Bruce Richard Crain was born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, on September 10, 1962. He received the BS degree in electrical engineering from Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, in 1984, and the MS degree in electrical engineering from the Florida Institute of Technology, Melbourne, in 1989. He is currently working toward the PhD in electrical engineering from the Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta. From 1984 to 1986 he worked at Harris Corp., Melbourne, Florida, where he designed avionics equipment for compliance with electromagnetic interference (EMI) requirements. From 1986 to 1989, he worked as an electromagnetic environmental effects (E3) engineer for Grumman Melbourne Systems, Melbourne, where he performed extensive computer-aided electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) analyses for military aircraft. From 1989 to 1990, he worked as an EMC consultant to Alenia Spazio in Turin, Italy, in support of various scientific satellite systems. From 1990 to 1992, he worked as an EMC consultant to Matra Marconi Space, Toulouse, France, where he supported development of several earth observation satellites. From 1992 to 1994, he was a graduate research assistant with the Georgia Tech Research Institute, Atlanta, where he developed EMC analysis computer codes. Currently, he is working at Lockheed Aeronautical Systems Company, Atlanta, as the lead E3 engineer for the development of the next generation of Hercules transport aircraft. He is a member of Eta Kappa Nu and the IEEE EMC and M l T Societies. He is also a NARTE certified EMC engineer and a professional engineer registered with the state of Florida. His current research interests are the application of vector finite element methods to the solution of unbounded waveguide problems, particularly ferrite-loaded waveguides
